:::{#exm-deriv-dot-product}
#### Example of the dot-product rule

Apply @thm-deriv-dot-product with the vector $\vcoef = \tp{(\coef{1}, \coef{2})}$
in the role of $\vx$.
Let $\vecf{a}(\vcoef) = \tp{(\coef{1}, \coef{1}\coef{2})}$
and $\vecf{b}(\vcoef) = \tp{(\coef{2}, \coef{1})}$.
Then:

$$
\vecf{a} \cdot \vecf{b}
= \coef{1} \cdot \coef{2} + \coef{1}\coef{2} \cdot \coef{1}
= \coef{1}\coef{2} + \coef{1}^2\coef{2}
$$

By direct calculation:

$$
\underbrace{\deriv{\vcoef}(\vecf{a} \cdot \vecf{b})}_{2 \times 1}
= \deriv{\vcoef}(\coef{1}\coef{2} + \coef{1}^2\coef{2})
= \begin{pmatrix} \coef{2} + 2\coef{1}\coef{2} \\ \coef{1} + \coef{1}^2 \end{pmatrix}
$$

By the product rule (@thm-deriv-dot-product),
using
$\underbrace{\deriv{\vcoef}\tp{\vecf{a}}}_{2 \times 2}
= \begin{pmatrix}1 & \coef{2} \\ 0 & \coef{1}\end{pmatrix}$
and
$\underbrace{\deriv{\vcoef}\tp{\vecf{b}}}_{2 \times 2}
= \begin{pmatrix}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{pmatrix}$:

$$
\ba
\underbrace{\deriv{\vcoef}(\vecf{a} \cdot \vecf{b})}_{2 \times 1}
&=
\underbrace{\begin{pmatrix}1 & \coef{2} \\ 0 & \coef{1}\end{pmatrix}}_{2 \times 2}
\underbrace{\begin{pmatrix}\coef{2} \\ \coef{1}\end{pmatrix}}_{2 \times 1}
+
\underbrace{\begin{pmatrix}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{pmatrix}}_{2 \times 2}
\underbrace{\begin{pmatrix}\coef{1} \\ \coef{1}\coef{2}\end{pmatrix}}_{2 \times 1}
\\
&=
\begin{pmatrix}\coef{2} + \coef{1}\coef{2} \\ \coef{1}^2\end{pmatrix}
+
\begin{pmatrix}\coef{1}\coef{2} \\ \coef{1}\end{pmatrix}
\\
&=
\begin{pmatrix}\coef{2} + 2\coef{1}\coef{2} \\ \coef{1}^2 + \coef{1}\end{pmatrix}
\ea
$$

Both methods agree.

:::
